Migration of pain

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 20-year-old man develops vague periumbilical discomfort followed several hours later by focal right lower quadrant pain, anorexia and nausea. Examination now shows localized guarding. Which process best explains the change in pain localization?

  1. Resolution of inflammation without local irritation
  2. An isolated injury to the left sciatic nerve
  3. A purely psychogenic change in pain reporting
  4. Referred pain from the shoulder
  5. Progression from visceral pain to irritation of parietal peritoneum
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Progression from visceral pain to irritation of parietal peritoneum

Early visceral pain is poorly localized; local parietal peritoneal irritation produces focal pain.

Understanding the options

Progression from visceral pain to irritation of parietal peritoneum
Early visceral pain is poorly localized; local parietal peritoneal irritation produces focal pain.
Resolution of inflammation without local irritation
The new guarding suggests progression rather than resolution.
An isolated injury to the left sciatic nerve
This does not match the abdominal pain pattern.
A purely psychogenic change in pain reporting
The temporal pattern and guarding have a physiologic explanation.
Referred pain from the shoulder
This does not explain the classic periumbilical-to-right-lower-quadrant sequence.
